calibration.calibration_cost_note: Monte Carlo under an assumed model, not physically acquired. Directly collecting this many128s histories would take20.74days at default counts, plus3.2h response scan. A practical laboratory calibration protocol is still needed.
calibration.decision: abs(calibrated linear estimate)>independently calibrated threshold; power uses abs(relative-power change)

resource_ledger.matched: acquisition duration, source paths and target task; assumed photon allotment bookkeeping only
not_matched: atomic cooling, trapping, readout and reset light
resource_ledger.coupling_assumption: The atomic geometry/coupling is assumed calibrated to a pi/2 pulse in2.5ms at its45% allocation. Dipole/beam-area coupling and apparatus are unmodeled; varying allotted photons alone does not change Omega. No measured device/coupling validation.
resource_ledger.photon_accounting_limit: A source-photon-allocation check is not total-resource fairness or proof of quantum advantage.

scope: Low-frequency narrow-line698nm laboratory surrogate, not193nm DUV, CO2 drive or13.5nm EUV.
64 independent atoms with classical optical drive, no squeezing/entanglement.
Interrogation samples once per second; source frequency is quasi-static within each25ms window.
No phase-noise spectrum reconstruction, wafer outcome, real sensor performance or end-to-end quantum advantage established.

sources.title: Bishof et al., Optical spectrum analyzer with quantum limited noise floor (2013)
sources.role: Established atomic laser-noise spectroscopy; quadrature Ramsey, finite pulses and dead-time precedent. Our numerical values/results are synthetic.

sources.role: Laser noise can limit atomic-qubit control; not validation of this surrogate.
